title: Scalar source tests from compact logarithmic kernels
source_hypothesis: Every d>=0; bounded full boundary-kernel families with common compact projections. Finite-order scalar reduction additionally requires a cutoff equal to one on the whole input projection and a containing base-frequency rectangle compactly inside the permitted cone.
reviewed_arguments: D0 states bounded complete operator families, every dimension d>=0, fixed compact projections, and the whole-input product-cone condition required only for finite-order scalar domination.
D1 proves the exact logarithmic L2 unitary, the Schwartz image of smooth boundary inputs and the t^(1/2) kernel factor with s=-log(t).

D2 uses the full conormal normal reduction near the diagonal and proves uniform all-derivative exponential side-tail bounds before taking the full logarithmic Fourier symbol. No residual kernel is omitted.

D3 constructs a strictly positive Schwartz frequency floor from lattice translates of a squared Fourier transform. Its inverse kernel is the actual compact autocorrelation times an all-derivative convergent Fourier series.

D4 takes a fixed root of a rapidly decreasing envelope and proves every reciprocal derivative bound needed by the exact 4(n+1)-derivative packet theorem. The quotient is used as an L2 operator, not asserted to belong to the full boundary calculus.

D5 proves exact right factorization, with the input cutoff in the correct position, and verifies the complete compact residual boundary kernel including both side faces and the corner. There is no positive tangential-dimension assumption.

D6 uses positive convolution to compactify the elliptic multiplier kernel while retaining its exact order, ellipticity and all-derivative off-cone rapid bounds. The autocorrelation product identity is justified distributionally.

D7 retains all numerator factors in the reciprocal derivative formula. The extra frequency weight absorbs their finite order and gives uniform bounded quotient derivatives both inside and outside the elliptic cone.
D8 proves one actual scalar compact finite-order test, its full microsupport, and the exact operator inequality for every family member.

D9 checks the entire input support of the finite source tree, not just its compressed microsupport. One order-zero scalar test then controls the local regularized H2 graph, actual equation and both traces, with graph limits identified by earlier flat transposes.

D10 preserves the product-patch limitation for finite-order tests. Global all-patch scalar source and observation assembly, other local regimes, the full parameter theorem and the wave application remain unfinished.

Three complete solutions verify the exact support wedge and density, all root and reciprocal exponents, and the order of the actual right factorization. The figure labels the allowed support region rather than kernel values.

All fifteen reader captures were inspected: twelve overlapping desktop views, the full figure and two mobile samples. Thirty-three exact checks, 265 formulas and 35 displays support the analytic receiving review.

Fifteen proof entries bind to 569 earlier entries in 25 maps, including 102 external Lebl proof nodes. Prior valid alternative proofs and current component licences are retained. Internal export proof closure and full-course completion are not claimed.
